headline: Large-denomination certificates of deposit: a wave of reissuance is spreading
summary: Bank of China restarted issuing long-term large-denomination certificates of deposit on July 1. Three- and five-year certificates from major state-owned banks have returned, paying noticeably higher rates than ordinary fixed deposits.
why: Certificates of deposit are bank-issued time deposits, and their pricing signals how banks are competing for funding. Changes in deposit rates affect bank margins and household savings behaviour.
